title: Quota cooldowns already existed in the engine; the bootstrap audit and FAIL-0001 missed them
summary: engine.py already wrote machine-wide quota cooldowns (provider-cooldowns.json) with a parsed reset time ('try again at H:MM PM') and removed cooling providers from availability. The Haiku runtime audit (EVR-0002) and FAIL-0001 both stated reset times were not captured. The real gaps were narrower: only one message format parsed, delegate/eval ignored cooldowns (so the bootstrap wasted two Luna calls), and no breaker for repeated unavailable failures. Lesson: 'check the existing capability first' applies to our own code as much as to open-source prior art; audits by cheap models need grep verification of 'missing' claims.
